perturbation.description: Retain every UK submission rather than only the first submission per UniqueID.
perturbation.why_plausible: A changed row-number predicate silently disables the duplicate-exclusion rule.

lossless_edits: Set the working directory to Study 2 and load tidyverse, readxl and knitr for the selected author-written numerical sections. No raw-data, exclusion, recode or model edits in the original run.
execution_scope: Study2_OSF_deidentified.Rmd lines 74–192 (raw-to-clean Study 2A), 258–263 (author-written percentage-gain aggregation), 324–327 (lmS2a), and 350–356 (lmS2a3). C3/C4 are Monetary:Country_UK coefficient/t; C5/C6 are tempS2a marGain percentages; C7 is FlatFee:Country_UK. For C8 use the authors' Welch t.test from lines 1860–1861 on the Study 2A UK Monetary/Norm subset. This is the same subset selected by the later across-study loop; other countries/studies cannot enter this test. Bootsrap intervals, plots and Studies 2B/2C are outside scope.
hard_coding_signal: Restore row_number() == 1 for UK submissions, removing the repeated records from the twin analysis.
notes: Every reference is from the logged local execution, not copied from a paper or a shipped rendered output.
Affected claims are defined by changes at printed precision, not by arbitrary raw floating-point differences. Unaffected claims retain gold statuses; their references are the actual twin run values.
R4 repairs are listed separately; twin.patch contains exactly one planted change against the pinned original file.
Only the numerical scope needed for all gold claims was executed; this is not an end-to-end run of every package output.

The omitted China-data pin is supplied in input_manifest.json as original OSF version 1 with SHA-256 aa31cfe5ef9ce27725b595cd257e27cee236ae657f8aa485c47cb50efd192bcb. The original run reproduces every claim. C7 is the secondary specific flat-fee contrast; C8 is the secondary Welch cost-effectiveness test. C6 uses China only and is unchanged.
